summary: This Dockerfile creates a Docker image that builds a Docusaurus website and serves it with nginx. It uses a multi-stage build process: first creating a base Node.js image, then using that to build the Docusaurus site, and finally copying only the built files into a lightweight nginx image for production.

explanations.1: This special comment tells Docker to use an enhanced Dockerfile parser that supports newer syntax features.
explanations.7: This starts with a Node.js image on Alpine Linux (a tiny Linux distribution) and names this stage 'base' so later stages can reference it.
explanations.10: This environment variable tells yarn to not use colored output in logs, making them easier to read and parse.
explanations.13: Corepack is Node's built-in package manager manager; enabling it lets you use yarn without installing it separately.
explanations.19: This creates a new build stage called 'building_production' that starts from the 'base' stage we created earlier.
explanations.22: This command creates a new Docusaurus project scaffolding directly into the Docker image rather than copying it from your computer.
explanations.25: After creating the Docusaurus files, this changes ownership so the 'node' user (instead of root) owns them, which is a security best practice.
explanations.31: This copies your package.json and yarn.lock files from your computer into the image before installing dependencies — Docker caches this layer, so if source code changes but dependencies don't, Docker can reuse the cached dependencies.
explanations.34: The --immutable flag makes yarn fail if the lock file doesn't match package.json, ensuring everyone builds with identical versions.
explanations.37: Now that dependencies are installed, this copies your actual source code files into the image.
explanations.40: This runs the build script to generate the final static HTML files that will be served.
explanations.46: This starts a completely new image stage based on nginx, which is a lightweight web server; we're not carrying over Node.js or build tools into production.
explanations.49: This copies only the built website files (the static HTML/CSS/JS) from the previous build stage into nginx's default directory, leaving behind all the build tools and source code.
